question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch Treaties and Contacts — Ruler and Region]
options: Sultan of Golconda — Granted golden firman for Masulipatnam factory
Marthanda Varma — Ruler of Travancore who engaged in war and defeated the Dutch
Zamorin of Calicut — Signed treaty allowing Dutch trade and military alliance against Portuguese
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj — Formed an alliance with the Dutch to jointly rule Goa
wrong_fact: Shivaji Maharaj did not form an alliance with the Dutch to jointly rule Goa. While Shivaji had commercial interactions with the Dutch (such as at Vengurla) and wanted to expel the Portuguese, there was never a joint rule or military alliance for Goa, which remained under Portuguese control.
explanation: The Qutb Shahi Sultan of Golconda granted permissions to the Dutch at Masulipatnam. Marthanda Varma of Travancore famously defeated the Dutch at Colachel in 1741. The Zamorin of Calicut partnered with the Dutch against their common Portuguese enemy. However, Shivaji Maharaj never formed an alliance to jointly rule Goa with the Dutch.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch Wars and Political Treaties — Event and Consequence]
options: Treaty of Mavelikkara (1753) — Dutch agreed to remain neutral and not interfere in Travancore's expansion
Capture of Cochin (1663) — Dutch ousted the Portuguese and installed a puppet ruler on the Cochin throne
Treaty of 1610 with Nayaka of Gingee — Allowed the Dutch to build Fort Geldria at Pulicat
Treaty of Pulicat (1690) — Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb directly ceded Madras to the Dutch
wrong_fact: There was no Treaty of Pulicat in 1690 where Aurangzeb ceded Madras to the Dutch. Madras (Fort St. George) was a British stronghold and was never ceded to the Dutch. Aurangzeb did issue firmans to the Dutch for trade in various regions, but Madras remained British.
explanation: The Treaty of Mavelikkara in 1753 formally sealed the peace between Travancore and the VOC, neutralizing Dutch political power on the Malabar Coast. In 1663, the Dutch captured Cochin and crowned a friendly local prince. In 1610, the Nayaka of Gingee allowed the Dutch to establish Fort Geldria at Pulicat. The claim that Aurangzeb ceded Madras to the Dutch is completely false.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch-Indian Geopolitics — Ruler, Settlement, and Conflict]
options: Venkatapata Deva Raya II (Aravidu Dynasty) — Allowed Dutch settlement at Pulicat despite Portuguese protests
Shah Jahan — Allowed the Dutch to establish a factory at Pipli in Odisha (1627)
Vijayappa Nayaka of Tanjore — Allowed the Dutch to build Fort Vijaya at Porto Novo
Ekoji I (Thanjavur Maratha) — Formed a defensive pact with the Dutch to partition Madurai
wrong_fact: Ekoji I of Thanjavur did not form a defensive pact with the Dutch to partition Madurai. While Ekoji I had relations with the Dutch (who held Nagapattinam in Tanjore territory), there was no joint pact or campaign to partition the neighboring Madurai Nayakdom.
explanation: Venkatapata Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara allowed the Dutch at Pulicat in 1610. Shah Jahan permitted the Pipli settlement in Odisha. Vijayappa Nayaka of Tanjore granted Porto Novo (Parangipettai) to the Dutch. Ekoji I confirmed Dutch rights at Nagapattinam but did not form a pact to partition Madurai.
